1.why: authenticatedSession() enforces session.accountId === account.id on every MFA route via requireAuth, and body() rejects any client-supplied accountId/userId, so settings are bound to the signed-in user.

2.why: Verification is bound to the single account's AES-GCM-encrypted secret and only checked inside that account's authenticated session, so no code can be applied to any other user — the statement is false.

3.why: The /api/mfa/verify handler sets mfaEnabled=true without rotating or invalidating the session, so the enabling session (and any prior sessions) remain valid — the statement is true.

4.why: The TOTP secret is stored via encrypt() (AES-256-GCM) in encryptedSecret and recovery codes likewise in encryptedRecoveryCodes; nothing is stored in plaintext.

5.why: Session IDs, CSRF tokens, the Base32 secret, recovery codes, IVs, and the master key are all derived from crypto.randomBytes, a CSPRNG.

6.why: The client keeps the CSRF token, secret, OTP, and codes only in in-memory JS variables, uses no localStorage/sessionStorage, and the sole cookie (mfa_session) is HttpOnly.

7.why: Server-side validEmail/validPhone/validOtp/validCode regex validators, content-type and 4KB body limits, and timing-safe comparisons validate all user input.

8.why: All dynamic values are inserted via textContent/createTextNode, innerHTML is used only with static templates, and a nonce-based CSP blocks injected script execution.

9.why: The server issues no HTTP redirects at all (no 3xx/Location and no redirect parameters), so no open redirect exists, though there is no explicit redirect allow-list mechanism.

10.why: headers() applies HSTS, a CSP with frame-ancestors 'none', X-Content-Type-Options: nosniff, and X-Frame-Options: DENY to every response including errors and OPTIONS.

11.why: cookie() sets the session cookie with HttpOnly, Secure, and SameSite=Strict (plus Max-Age), and clearCookie mirrors these attributes.

12.why: The client log() function writes the TOTP manual secret, the live six-digit OTP, and all recovery codes into the on-page 'Logs' panel and console.log, even though server errors are generic and stack traces are hidden.

13.why: TOTPs are 30-second-window codes with monotonic acceptedCounter replay rejection, and recovery codes are deleted on use and expire after 30 days.

14.why: failed()/locked() enforce a 10-minute lockout after 5 consecutive failed OTP or recovery-code verification attempts, returning 429.

15.why: Sign-in deletes the preauth session and issues a fresh session ID, 20-minute idle and 8-hour absolute timeouts are enforced in authenticatedSession, and logout deletes the session and clears the cookie.
